problem:
Northgate Retail, a fictional retailer, pays a supplier in US dollars while its operating account is in euro. The finance manager opens the bank app, sees a rate, accepts it, and expects the supplier to receive the agreed dollar amount. Instead the supplier is credited a different amount, the finance manager cannot reconcile the invoice, and the bank receives a complaint that the rate shown was not the rate applied.

The root cause is not a single wrong rate. The quote, the fee, the rate validity window and the execution moment are held in different places, and none of them is bound to the payment as one contract. A quote can expire while screening or routing is still running, a fee can be added after the quote screen, and a future dated instruction can execute on a day when one participant is closed. The customer sees a rate; the bank executes a different economic outcome.

Northgate Retail needs the bank to define the rate quote, the fees, the rate validity, the customer disclosure and the execution rules as one transparent package, so the amount the customer accepts is the amount that executes or the payment stops and asks again.
solution:
Bind the quote to the payment as a single snapshot: quote ID, currency pair, buy and sell amounts, rate, spread, each fee, the total debit, the total credit, the expiry timestamp and the execution conditions. Show the customer the full disclosure before acceptance, including the rate, the fee breakdown, the exact amount the beneficiary will receive and how long the quote is valid. Store that snapshot and the consent evidence with the payment record so any later dispute can be reconstructed exactly.

Revalidate the quote at execution. If the quote has expired, if the rate or amount has moved beyond the agreed tolerance, or if liquidity for the settlement currency is not available, pause execution and obtain a fresh quote and fresh consent. Never execute at a different rate silently. If the customer declines the new quote, cancel the instruction cleanly with no debit and a clear audit record.

Handle dates explicitly. Apply the scheme, currency, debtor bank, creditor bank and clearing calendars to any future dated instruction, and show the customer the calculated execution date and the rule that produced it when the requested date is not an eligible processing day. Store the requested date, the calculated date, the calendar source and version, and the timezone separately.

Design the cover and customer legs as separately tracked legs where a correspondent model is used. A cover return must not automatically change the customer leg status; correlate both legs by stable references, determine the customer leg state first, and only then decide the customer impact. That separation protects the customer from an internal settlement event they did not cause.

decision.question: A Northgate Retail finance manager accepts a euro to US dollar quote valid for 30 seconds. Screening takes longer than expected and the payment reaches execution 90 seconds after acceptance, when the market rate has moved. The supplier invoice is for a fixed dollar amount. What should the bank do?

options.label: A
options.detail: Execute at the old rate and absorb the difference silently in a suspense account.

options.label: B
options.detail: Cancel the supplier payment and convert the euro amount into dollars at the next available rate without consent.

options.label: C
options.detail: Execute at the new market rate without telling the customer, since the payment was already authorised.

options.label: D
options.detail: Stop execution, do not apply a different rate silently, and ask the customer to accept a fresh quote with the new rate, fees and final amounts disclosed before execution.

decisionRationale: Option D is correct because the quote, rate, expiry and execution conditions form one contract, and a payment must not be silently executed at a different rate. Option C is wrong because it changes the agreed economics without consent. Option A is wrong because absorbing the difference hides the true cost and breaks reconciliation. Option B is wrong because it cancels and re-executes without the customer agreeing the new terms.

steps.title: Enters supplier, dollar amount and requested date in the banking channel
Returns a quote with rate, fees, total debit, total credit and a 30 second validity window
Reviews the full disclosure and accepts the quote
Binds the quote snapshot and consent to the payment and checks calendars and limits
Runs sanctions, AML and fraud screening within the execution window
Revalidates the quote at execution and checks settlement currency liquidity
Executes the conversion and sends the payment and any cover leg
Confirms the final amounts, rate and value date to the customer and the supplier reference

happy: The finance manager accepts a quote with the rate, fees and final dollar credit fully disclosed. Screening completes inside the validity window, the quote revalidates at execution, the conversion executes at the accepted rate, the supplier receives the agreed dollar amount, and the confirmation shows the rate, fees, value date and quote ID for reconciliation.

negative.title: Quote expires before execution
negative.detail: Screening or routing delays execution beyond the quote validity window. Pause execution, present a fresh quote with new rate and amounts, and proceed only on fresh consent or cancel cleanly with no debit.

negative.title: Future date falls on a non processing day
negative.detail: The requested execution date is a holiday for one participant in the chain. Apply the documented calendar adjustment rule, show the customer the calculated date and the reason, and store requested and calculated dates separately.

negative.title: Cover leg returned while customer leg is unclear
negative.detail: A pacs.009 cover leg is returned but the customer pacs.008 leg state is not yet known. Correlate both legs by stable references, establish the customer leg state before any customer adjustment, and investigate rather than assuming one leg defines the other.

negative.title: FX quote service unavailable
negative.detail: No live quote can be obtained at instruction time. Do not invent a rate or reuse a stale quote; tell the customer the service is unavailable and offer to retry or to schedule the instruction when quoting resumes.

technical: Store the quote as an immutable snapshot with quote ID, currency pair, rate, amounts, fees, spread, expiry timestamp, tolerance and consent timestamp, linked to the payment by correlation ID. Enforce single consumption of a quote so one quote cannot fund two payments. Validate amounts and currency codes, apply rounding rules consistently between quote and execution, and record the calendar source and version used for any date adjustment. Keep customer leg and cover leg records separate with linked transaction IDs and, where applicable, the UETR, so each leg has its own state machine and audit trail. Log every revalidation, expiry and fresh consent as an event.

messages.title: Customer payment initiation carrying the instruction and references
Customer credit transfer for the converted payment
Cover leg for settlement through the correspondent chain where the cover model is used
Status report for each leg so acceptance and rejection are tracked separately

accounting: Debit the customer euro account for the total agreed debit, credit the FX conversion account at the quoted rate, and credit the settlement account for the dollar amount, with fees posted as separate entries so the principal, the rate and the fee are each reconcilable. If the quote expires and the customer declines a fresh quote, reverse any reservation exactly once and leave no partial conversion posting. A returned cover leg goes to a nostro reconciliation and investigation worklist; the customer leg is only adjusted once its own state is established. Operations monitor quote expiry rates, revalidation failures and cover return ageing as service quality measures.

scenarios.given: a customer has accepted an FX quote with a defined expiry
scenarios.when: execution is attempted after the quote has expired
scenarios.then: the payment is not silently executed at a different rate. the customer is asked to accept a fresh quote or cancel

scenarios.given: a future dated payment falls on a non processing day
scenarios.when: the scheduler evaluates the requested date
scenarios.then: the documented date adjustment policy is applied. the customer is shown the calculated execution date

questions.question: What must a payment never do when an FX quote has expired before execution?
options: Show the customer the new rate
Execute silently at a different rate
Pause and seek a fresh quote and consent
questions.explanation: An expired quote must not lead to silent execution at a different rate; the customer must accept fresh terms.

questions.question: Which items should be bound to the payment as one FX quote snapshot?
options: Quote ID, currency pair, amounts, rate, fees, expiry and execution conditions
questions.explanation: The quote contract includes the ID, pair, amounts, rate, fees, spread, expiry and execution conditions.

questions.question: What should happen when a cover leg is returned but the customer leg status is unclear?
options: Investigate both legs before posting a customer adjustment
questions.explanation: Cover and customer leg states must be modelled separately and investigated before any customer adjustment.

questions.question: How should a future dated payment on a non processing day be handled?
options: Execute it on the requested date anyway
Apply the documented calendar adjustment and show the calculated date
Move it silently to the next month
questions.explanation: The correct scheme and participant calendars govern the date, and the adjustment must be transparent to the customer.
